docs.title: FSM-LLM
docs.text:
Covers FSM-LLM v0.13.0

Stateful conversational AI: you describe a conversation as a finite state machine in JSON, and a language model does the language work inside each state.

A language model call starts from nothing. A multi-turn conversation that must collect data, follow a set flow and decide the same way every time needs structure around the model. FSM-LLM splits the work three ways: the model understands the user, pulls out facts and writes replies; the state machine decides where the conversation goes next by rules, not by mood; the framework keeps the state, the history, your hooks and the saved sessions.

It is one package, fsm_llm, with a small core and seven subpackages on top: reasoning strategies, a workflow engine, 18 agent patterns, a monitoring dashboard, an evaluation harness, runtime FSM synthesis and public test doubles. Every subpackage is built from the same parts as the core (stacked FSMs, message-free steps, one LLM layer), so there is one way to run a model.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pip install llm-fsm

The distribution is llm-fsm and the import package is fsm_llm. Python 3.11 or newer. fsm-llm on PyPI is a different, unrelated project: if you installed it by mistake, run pip uninstall fsm-llm first. The Quick Start covers the extras and the model setting.

docs.title: The shortest working example
docs.text:
This runs with no model and no network: a scripted model double from fsm_llm.testing stands in for the LLM. With a real model you drop the double and pass model= (or set LLM_MODEL).

from fsm_llm import API
from fsm_llm.testing import ScriptedLLM

greeter = {
    "name": "Greeter",
    "description": "Learns the user's name, then says goodbye",
    "initial_state": "ask_name",
    "states": {
        "ask_name": {
            "id": "ask_name",
            "description": "Find out the user's name",
            "purpose": "Learn the user's name",
            "extraction_instructions": "Extract the user's name if they gave it",
            "response_instructions": "Ask for the user's name",
            "required_context_keys": ["name"],
            "transitions": [
                {
                    "target_state": "goodbye",
                    "description": "The name is known",
                    "conditions": [
                        {
                            "description": "A name was collected",
                            "requires_context_keys": ["name"],
                            "logic": {"has_context": "name"},
                        }
                    ],
                }
            ],
        },
        "goodbye": {
            "id": "goodbye",
            "description": "Say goodbye",
            "purpose": "Wrap up the conversation",
            "response_instructions": "Say goodbye by name",
        },
    },
}

llm = ScriptedLLM(
    extraction_data={"name": "Alice"},
    responses={"ask_name": "What is your name?", "goodbye": "Goodbye, Alice!"},
)
api = API.from_definition(greeter, llm_interface=llm)
conversation_id, opening = api.start_conversation()
print(opening)                                      # What is your name?
print(api.converse("I am Alice", conversation_id))  # Goodbye, Alice!
print(api.get_data(conversation_id), api.get_current_state(conversation_id))

The conversation starts in ask_name, the extraction fills name, the transition condition passes, and the reply is written from the state the conversation ended in, goodbye. The Quick Start runs the same shape against a real model.

docs.title: The subpackages
docs.text:
Each subpackage is imported by name (from fsm_llm.agents import create_agent); import fsm_llm loads only the core. Their usage is in the API Reference, and each has a README with its own guide:

docs.title: 1. Executive summary
docs.text:
Positioning. fsm_llm is the framework for deterministic, durable, auditable conversational state machines with grounded retrieval. txtai is a retrieval and pipeline platform whose agents run a smolagents loop. deepseek-harness is a durable, plugin-first agent runtime whose control flow is an open model loop or a model-written program. NOOA makes an agent a Python object whose ... methods an LLM completes, with control flow in ordinary Python. None of the three offers rule-based, statically checkable, replayable dialogue control. That is the moat. Every item below widens it or removes a reason not to adopt the library.

In one line: NOOA makes an agent a Python object; fsm_llm makes a conversation a verifiable, durable state machine, which can also be written as a Python object that compiles to one, or be compiled at runtime from a goal.

State of play. Runtime FSM synthesis, the v2.1 flagship, shipped in v0.12.0 as fsm_llm.synthesis with gates G1 to G7, a content-addressed library, a runner and a repair loop. Its pre-registered benchmark ran three blocks, all INCONCLUSIVE: one model played every role, so the central claim (a frontier model compiles, a small model executes) is still untested. The platform under it (event log, async core, context engineering, serving) is still the v2.1 gap list.

Nine moves, in order of leverage:

# Move Where 1 Make it installable and consistent: PyPI, Python 3.11 to 3.15, standard layout, small modules, public test doubles, a versioned schema registry, one reason-code vocabulary Phase 0 2 Make execution durable: an append-only event log as the single source of truth, async core, crash-safe resume, fork, core turn budgets Phase 1 3 Engineer the context window: values by reference, a cache-stable prompt layout, a token meter; compaction only as a logged fallback Phase 2 4 Ground conversations in evidence: txtai retrieval, calibrated evidence and decision confidence as handler-only routing facts Phase 3 5 Make authoring Pythonic without losing verification: typed context schema, FSM classes that compile to the JSON IR Workstream O 6 Harden agents: one policy object, a sandbox, code as action as a state kind Phase 4 7 Serve and interoperate on current standards: Open Responses, MCP 2026-07-28 with stateless slot filling, A2A v1.0.1, AG-UI 1.0 Phase 5 8 Prove quality: three-model nightly matrix, one shared simulator, pre-registered benchmarks Phase 6 9 Harden runtime synthesis and run the experiment that can support or falsify it Phase 7

What changed in v3.0 (full list in Section 14):

  • Section 2 is new: ten contracts every phase builds on, so features compose instead of accumulating.
  • Phase 7 is rewritten from a build plan into a status report plus remaining work (P7.1 to P7.9).
  • Five design defects in v2.1 are fixed: the cache layout, the layering rules, spoofable routing facts, uncalibrated score thresholds, and compaction versus append-only history.
  • External targets are updated: MCP 2026-07-28 (stateless, MRTR), A2A v1.0.1, Open Responses, OTel GenAI conventions in their new repository, ATIF v1.8, AG-UI 1.0, Python 3.11 end of life in October 2027.
  • All effort and calendar estimates are removed.

docs.title: 2. Core contracts
docs.text:
Every phase builds on these ten contracts. A feature that needs something outside them extends a contract (with a recorded schema or format version) or is out of scope. Each row names the items that build the contract and the items that consume it.

ID Contract Definition Built by Consumed by C1 FSM definition IR FSM JSON (FSMDefinition) is the one canonical program. JSON files, Python builders, Python classes (Workstream O) and synthesizer output are front ends that compile to it. A schema registry records the version that introduced every field 0.12, O1 Verifier, visualizer, engine, synthesis, oo C2 State kinds and executors A state has exactly one kind, derived from which config it carries: conversation (default, Pass 1 and Pass 2), completion (exists), synthesize (exists), reply (new, deterministic template), codeact (new). Each kind declares its config model, the handler-only result key it writes, its read and write sets for G3, its liveness rule for G4, its sample values for G6a, and an executor. The executor protocol lives in core, so executors at any layer can implement it; the registry lives in engine 0.14, P7.1, O2, 3.4, 4.4 Engine, verifier, oo, synthesis C3 Context namespaces Three key classes. Public keys: extractable, typed by context_schema. Handler-only keys: written only by executors and handlers, never by extraction (exists as handler_only_names()). Internal keys: prefixes _, system_, internal_, __, never shown to a model. Every runtime fact that routing reads is a handler-only <kind>_result dict with a status: completion result (exists), synthesis_result (exists), retrieval_result, decision_result, codeact_result 3.4, 3.9, 4.4 JsonLogic routing, verifier G3 C4 Event log Append-only, versioned, one log per conversation tree. Every model-visible input is an event; large payloads are content-addressed blobs; value references point into blobs. Two privacy levels: shape (names, types, codes, counts; today's synthesis trace contract) and values (opt-in, secrets filtered at write). Sessions, monitor, token meter, OTel, ATIF, usage, synthesis traces and library counters are projections 1.1 to 1.13 Everything above runtime C5 LLM interface One LLMInterface with sync methods and async mirrors. Native providers speak Open Responses and Anthropic Messages; litellm is an optional provider. Retry and admission control wrap the interface, not individual providers. Usage is a projection of events, not a counter 1.5, 1.6, 1.13, 5.4 Engine, agents, synthesis C6 Verifier One module runs G1 (loads), G2 (structure), G3 (data flow), G4 (liveness), G5 (policy) and G6a (dead edges) and returns one GateReport type. Used by fsm-llm-validate, API load, oo compile, the synthesizer and repair 0.4, M2 (shipped) CLI, engine, oo, synthesis C7 Simulator One goal- and persona-driven user simulator with a judge model separate from the executor. Used by G6b, evaluation, trace-to-eval, repair admission and benchmarks 6.6 Synthesis, eval C8 Reason codes One closed vocabulary of statuses (ok, failed, aborted, running, abstained) and reasons. Synthesis codes keep their wire values; agent stop reasons and approval outcomes map into it. Branch on codes, never on message text 0.13 Every *_result, AgentResult, approval, tools C9 Policy One policy object: approval mode (ask, never, auto), tool allowlist, sandbox profile, budgets (max_steps, max_seconds, tokens). SynthesisPolicy (kept by repo decision) is composed into it. Approvers are callables returning a coded outcome; a missing or failing approver fails closed; every request and outcome is an event 4.1, 4.2 Agents, engine executors, synthesis C10 Extension points Entry-point groups fsm_llm.providers, fsm_llm.stores, fsm_llm.state_kinds, fsm_llm.tools, fsm_llm.handlers. JSON references handlers and tools by registered name, which keeps G5's "no code in a definition" true and makes a JSON to class to JSON round trip exact 5.5, O2 Engine, oo, synthesis

Rules that follow from the contracts:

  1. Routing reads only public keys and handler-only <kind>_result facts. A routing input that extraction can write is a defect (C3).
  2. A new state behaviour is a new kind with an executor and verifier hooks, never a branch inside the turn pipeline (C2).
  3. A new runtime signal is an event first and a projection second; no subsystem keeps a private counter (C4).
  4. A new result type carries a C8 status and reason, not free text.
  5. A new definition field is registered with its schema version before it can load (C1).

docs.title: 3.1 Architecture snapshot
docs.text: Layer What exists Core turn Two passes per user message. Pass 1 extracts data; JsonLogic rules pick the transition in plain Python (lowest priority wins; the LLM is asked only when two or more rules tie at that priority; no passing rule means the conversation stays put). Pass 2 writes the reply from the resulting state. required_context_keys guides extraction but never blocks a transition. The prompt shows the last max_history_size messages (default 5) State kinds A state is a conversation state, a completion state (one complete call with tools or a response format, result in a handler-only key, skip-if-set) or a synthesize state (left BLOCKED by core; driven by fsm_llm.synthesis.ProcedureRunner) Verification FSMValidator (structure) and flow_analysis.py (G3 data flow, G4 liveness) in core; handler_only_names() shared by the pipeline and the analysis Composition API.push_fsm / API.pop_fsm with context passing and merge strategies; DEFAULT_MAX_STACK_DEPTH = 10 State SessionStore ABC with FileSessionStore (snapshots); context compaction by key (ContextCompactor) Subpackages reasoning; workflows (async, in memory, Python DSL, no JSON loader); agents (18 patterns plus AgentGraph, tools, HITL, MCP client, A2A, meta-builder, Agent Skills); monitor (FastAPI dashboard, OTel exporter); eval; synthesis (new in v0.12) Knowledge OKF bundles (okf.py), okf_bridge; SemanticMemoryStore CLIs 8 entry points: fsm-llm, -visualize, -validate, -monitor, -meta, -eval, -okf, -skills Core dependencies loguru, litellm (>=1.83.0,<2.0, pinned 1.102.1), pydantic, python-dotenv, tenacity (declared because litellm's sync retries import it), pyyaml Engineering practice Naming conventions for new code in AGENTS.md; # DECISION anchors resolved through an append-only manifest (plans/ANCHORS.md); benchmarks pre-registered with sha256 pins of the source they ran against (scripts/bench_data/)

docs.title: 3.3 Strengths to preserve
docs.text:
• Deterministic control. Rules decide transitions; the model extracts and talks. This must survive every refactor.
  • Verification in core. G3 and G4 already run over any FSMDefinition, not only generated ones.
  • One LLM layer. Core, reasoning, workflows, agents and synthesis all call models through LLMInterface.
  • Security posture. Internal key prefixes and secret-looking values stay out of prompts; approval grants cannot be forged by the model; handler-only keys cannot be written by extraction; OKF, skill and generated text carry untrusted labels; constraints.txt excludes the compromised litellm 1.82.7 and 1.82.8.
  • Evaluation honesty. Pre-registered blocks pinned to source hashes, Wilson intervals, inconclusive verdicts reported as such.
  • Offline test depth. 13,777 tests run without a model.

docs.title: 4.1 txtai
docs.text:
Master af8f0b0 declares 9.15.0, which is unreleased; the latest PyPI release is 9.14.0 (2026-10-06). 34,167 src lines, Python 3.11 or later. An embeddings database with pipelines, workflows, agents and an API, configured from one YAML file, with heavy dependencies behind extras. Since the v2.1 baseline: bug fixes, plus a check that an ANN backend supports upserts and deletes before data changes.

Feature Where in txtai Decision Item Embeddings database: dense, sparse and hybrid scoring, SQL over results, graph embeddings/, database/, scoring/, graph/ Integrate as an optional backend; do not reimplement 3.1 to 3.3 12 dense ANN backends (annoy, faiss, ggml, hnsw, milvus, numpy, pgvector, rabitq, sqlite, torch, turbovec, zvec) and 4 sparse (ivfsparse, milvus, pg, zvec) ann/dense, ann/sparse Inherit through the integration 3.1 Backend capability check (upsert, delete) before any write ann/base.py, embeddings/base.py Make capabilities part of the VectorStore protocol 3.2 Calibrated scores: Bayesian (BB25) sparse normalization to [0, 1]; hybrid fusion in log-odds space with per-query dense calibration scoring/sparse.py, scoring/normalize.py, embeddings/search/hybrid.py Evidence thresholds apply only to calibrated scores 3.5 Late interaction and MUVERA pooling models/pooling/ Inherit through the integration 3.1 RAG pipeline (similarity plus LLM, minimum score, context limits) pipeline/llm/rag.py Adopt the pattern as the retrieval attribute 3.4 Textractor, segmentation, reranker pipeline/data, pipeline/text Adopt for ingestion and reranking 3.6, 3.7 Agent on smolagents (CodeAgent, ToolCallingAgent); tools bash, edit, glob, grep, read, write, todo, skill, embeddings; agents.md and skill.md instruction files agent/ Adopt the toolset and instruction loading, not the loop 2.7, 4.3 YAML Application; FastAPI with an OpenAI-compatible router; MCP exposure through fastapi_mcp app/, api/ Adopt the single-file app; build MCP on the official SDK instead of fastapi_mcp 5.1 to 5.3 Workflow tasks with cron scheduling workflow/ Adopt scheduling only 5.7 LLM backends: Hugging Face, llama.cpp, LiteLLM, LiteRT, OpenCode pipeline/llm/ Skip; providers follow 5.4 none Audio, image, translation, training, ONNX export, cloud index sync various Skip none

Lesson to copy: one configuration file builds the whole application, every heavy capability is an extra that fails with a clear install hint, and scores that drive decisions are calibrated.

docs.title: 4.2 deepseek-harness
docs.text:
TypeScript monorepo of 383 packages (379 at the v2.1 baseline) plus a Python SDK; release line 0.2.2-rc.2. A plugin-first agent runtime (Cordis microkernel) with durable sessions, subagents, sandboxing and several clients. Since the v2.1 baseline (857 commits): PTC bootstrap protocol 3 with a persistent scoped-repl program format as the default for persistent execution; runtime-context reminders that append to the transcript instead of rewriting the request prefix; coded approval denials; read-only tools declared concurrency-safe; batch Session.append; session-scoped writable directories in the sandbox; an upgrade guide for every breaking change.

Feature Where in the harness Decision Item Append-only session log; "model-visible means logged" docs/architecture.md, packages/session/* Adopt as C4 1.1 Session format with adjacent migrations; JSONL persistence; projections; SQLite query; single and batch append packages/session/*, packages/session-query Adopt 1.1, 1.2 Checkpoint policy packages/session/session-checkpoint-policy Adopt 1.3 Retry with logged policy; explicit turn cancellation packages/llm/llm-retry Adopt 1.5, 1.6 OTel session telemetry packages/session/session-telemetry-otel Adopt over the event log 1.10 Replay and mock testing; "verify the world, not the self-report" packages/test-support/*, docs/testing.md Adopt 0.9, 1.9, 6.2 Token meter packages/llm/token-meter Adopt 2.1 Runtime-context records appended as reminders, so the existing request prefix is never rewritten docs/upgrade-guide/v0.2.2-rc.1/runtime-context-reminders Adopt for state changes, stack frames and compaction epochs 2.4 Compaction: basic, tool-result pruner packages/compaction/* Adopt as the fallback 2.5 Spill store with policy packages/spill/* Adopt as the storage side of value references 2.2 Repeat-tool reminder (3, 5, 8), timeout policy packages/guard/* Adopt 2.6 System prompt sections; agent instruction chain packages/core/system-prompt, packages/context Adopt 2.3, 2.7 User approval (ask, never), permission presets, auto-review, coded denials packages/interaction/*, packages/experimental/auto-review Adopt in C9 with C8 codes 4.1 Sandbox seam: local, policy, Windows ACL, session-scoped writable directories; docs.title: 4.3 NVIDIA Object-Oriented Agents (NOOA)
docs.text:
Unchanged since v2.1 at fd62a60. Paper arXiv:2607.20709 (22 July 2026); repository alpha, Apache-2.0, requires-python >=3.12,<3.14, no native Windows; 100,721 src lines plus 52,146 in sub-packages (cli, atom, memory, bench, acp). An agent is a Python class: methods are actions, fields are state, docstrings are prompts, type annotations are contracts. A method whose body is ... is completed by an LLM loop. NVIDIA reports, from its own comparisons, 82.2% on SWE-bench Verified with GPT-5.5 at about 1.1M tokens and 29 calls per task, against 2.2M tokens and 66 calls for comparison harnesses reaching 78.2%, with median sessions peaking at 22k to 72k prompt tokens and no compaction. NOOA has no conversation state machine and no static verification of control flow.

Lesson to copy: token savings come from keeping large values out of the prompt and keeping the transcript append-only and cache-valid.

docs.title: 4.5 Principles
docs.text:
1. Model-visible means logged. Every input the model sees is an event; every prompt can be rebuilt from the log.
  2. Fail closed. Missing approver, unknown tool outcome, unresolved prompt variable, unverified generated FSM: stop and report a code; never guess.
  3. Verify the world, not the self-report. Tests and evals check end state (FSM state, extracted context, side effects).
  4. Integrate, do not reimplement. Retrieval comes from txtai; protocols come from their official SDKs; fsm_llm owns control flow.
  5. Optional heavy dependencies. Core installs with pydantic, loguru and pyyaml; providers, retrieval, serving and telemetry are extras.
  6. Model proposes, Python disposes. Every model-produced value (extraction, decision, generated FSM, code result) is typed and checked by deterministic code before it takes effect.
  7. Pass by reference, keep prefixes stable. Large values stay out of prompts; prompts only grow at the end.
  8. One canonical IR. FSM JSON is the single input to verification, visualization, execution and synthesis.
  9. One contract per concept. One simulator, one verifier, one reason vocabulary, one policy object, one event log (Section 2).
  10. Shape by default, values by opt-in. Shared stores keep names, types, codes and counts; values need an explicit setting.

docs.title: 5.1 Package layout
docs.text:
src/fsm_llm/
├── __init__.py          # public API re-exports; unchanged import paths
├── core/                # pure: definitions and schema registry (C1), JsonLogic, transition evaluation,
│                        #   executor protocol (C2), flow analysis and verifier G1 to G6a (C6), reason codes (C8)
├── llm/                 # LLMInterface sync and async (C5), providers/ (open_responses, anthropic, litellm),
│                        #   parsing, model catalog, token meter
├── runtime/             # event log and blobs (C4), projections, stores, checkpoint, retry, admission,
│                        #   cancellation, fork, usage, exporters (otel, atif)
├── context/             # value references and previews, prompt layout (prefix, history, suffix),
│                        #   runtime-context records, compaction fallback, instruction loading
├── retrieval/           # VectorStore protocol, memory, txtai backend, retrieval executor, rerank
├── okf/                 # bundles, bridge, ingest
├── skills/              # layered skill registry
├── tools/               # ToolRegistry, ToolDefinition, MCP client adapters (moved down from agents)
├── policy/              # Policy (C9), approval, sandbox seam and backends
├── engine/              # turn pipeline (Pass 1, Pass 2), state-kind registry and executors (C2),
│                        #   stack, handlers, API facade
├── simulation/          # user simulator and judge (C7)
├── oo/                  # Python class front end
├── agents/              # patterns (incl. codeact executor), a2a, meta-builder
├── synthesis/           # synthesizer, library, synthesize executor, traces, repair
├── workflows/           # engine, persisted instances, schedules
├── reasoning/
├── serve/               # app.yml loader, Open Responses and Chat Completions routers, MCP server, AG-UI

docs.title: 5.2 Layering rules
docs.text:
Enforced in CI with an import-linter contract. Peers in one layer do not import each other; shared code moves down a layer.

Layer Packages May import L0 core security L1 llm L0 L2 runtime L0, L1 L3 context, retrieval, okf, skills, tools, policy L0 to L2 L4 engine L0 to L3 L5 simulation, oo L0 to L4 L6 agents, synthesis, workflows, reasoning L0 to L5 L7 serve, monitor, eval L0 to L6 none testing everything; never imported by the library

Consequences: the turn pipeline leaves core, which becomes pure and dependency-free (v2.1 let core import only security while it held a pipeline that calls models and emits events). synthesis stops importing agents, reasoning and eval, because ToolRegistry, approval and the simulator move to L3 and L5.

docs.title: 5.3 Turn lifecycle after Phases 1 and 2
docs.text:
user message
  → event turn/start
  → engine resolves the state kind and its executor (C2)
  → conversation kind:
      Pass 1: llm/request → llm/response → extraction (or extraction/miss, intent/out_of_scope)
      transition evaluation (rules evaluated, winner, tie-break with decision_result if any)
      handlers and tool calls (checkpoint before side effects)
      large results stored as blobs; prompts see bounded previews (C4)
      Pass 2: llm/request → llm/response
    other kinds: executor/start → executor events → executor/result (<kind>_result written, handler-only)
  → event turn/end
projections: session view, monitor, token meter, usage, OTel, ATIF, eval traces, synthesis traces

docs.title: 5.4 Prompt layout
docs.text:
Pass 1 and Pass 2 share the prefix. Within a conversation the prefix never changes and the history only grows; everything that changes per turn sits after the history.

Segment Content Changes when Prefix Root persona, policy text, tool schemas (union across states, sorted deterministically; per-state availability enforced by the executor, not by editing the list) Never within a conversation History User and assistant turns; runtime-context records for transitions, stack push and pop, and compaction epochs Appended only Suffix Pass task (extract fields or write the reply), current state instructions, a pushed child FSM's persona, current context, value previews Every request

A sliding history window (today's max_history_size) is replaced by epochs: history grows until the token meter crosses a threshold, then one compaction starts a new epoch (2.5).

docs.title: 6. Roadmap: Phases 0 to 6 and Workstream O
docs.text: Every item uses the same shape: what changes, where it lands, which contract (Section 2) it builds on or extends, and a test that proves it is done. Item numbers are sequential within a phase; Section 14.4 maps v2.1 numbers to v3.0 numbers.

docs.title: Phase 0: Foundation, distribution and contracts
docs.text:
Goal: anyone can pip install the library, the codebase is cheap to change, and the contracts that later phases extend exist.

# Change Where Builds on Done when 0.1 Publish to PyPI as llm-fsm (published by the author under the project's former name) after confirming account ownership; otherwise file a PEP 541 request for fsm-llm. The import name stays fsm_llm. Release on tag with trusted publishing, PEP 740 attestations and a CycloneDX SBOM pyproject.toml, .github/workflows/release.yml none pip install llm-fsm works on Linux, macOS and Windows; the README no longer says "install from a clone" 0.2 Support Python 3.11 to 3.15. Linux runs all five; macOS and Windows run 3.11 and 3.15. 3.11 is dropped at its end of life (October 2027) pyproject.toml, CI matrix none 9 green CI legs; classifiers match requires-python 0.3 Standard src/fsm_llm/ layout with packages.find; delete scripts/type_check.py; remove the logging shadowing risk repository root none mypy -p fsm_llm runs without symlinks; a wheel-content test passes 0.4 Split into the Section 5 layout. pipeline.py → engine/turn/{pass1,pass2,transitions,stack}; api.py → engine/api/{conversation,stack,sessions,run}; definitions.py → core/definitions/{state,transition,fsm,kinds,errors,results}; llm.py → llm/{interface,providers/litellm,parsing,usage}; prompts.py → context/layout/*; agents/fsm_definitions.py → one module per pattern; validator.py and flow_analysis.py → core/verify/; ToolRegistry → tools/; HITL → policy/ src/ Section 5 No module over 800 lines; public API snapshot (0.11) unchanged; the import-linter contract of Section 5.2 is green 0.5 Decision records: generate docs/decisions/index.md from plans/ANCHORS.md and the in-code anchors; CI fails on an anchor that does not resolve. CHANGELOG.md in Keep a Changelog form; every **BREAKING:** entry links an upgrade guide (Section 12) docs/decisions/, CHANGELOG.md, CI existing anchor manifest 100% of anchors resolve; comment share reported by CI, not gated 0.6 Fold the 14 audit-named test files (18,055 lines) into suites named after features; add a branch-coverage gate with a ratchet tests/, CI none No dated test files; coverage enforced and never decreasing 0.7 Documentation site: mkdocs-material with mkdocstrings, versioned per release; README trimmed to install, quickstart and links docs/, mkdocs.yml none Hosted docs build on every tag 0.8 Safe defaults: no silent default model (a clear error listing how to set one, or a small default); set LITELLM_MODE=PRODUCTION before litellm is imported and load .env only on explicit opt-in constants.py, llm/, CLI none A fresh install gives a clear message, never a silent 27B download; a stale .env cannot override an explicit setting 0.9 Public fsm_llm.testing: promote MockLLM2Interface and PromptGroundedLLM; add a scripted LLM (the pattern in synthesis/README.md), a scripted user, and assertions assert_state, assert_context, assert_path, assert_result(kind, status, reason) testing/ C8 Examples' tests and user projects use the public module 0.10 Supply chain: pip-audit or osv-scanner, dependency review, Actions pinned by SHA, the existing .pth audit. Declared ranges match tested pins (mcp>=2.2,<3, not >=1.0.0). A scheduled job proposes litellm and mcp pin refreshes, gated by the full suite CI, pyproject.toml, constraints.txt none A known-vulnerable dependency fails the build; no declared range admits an untested major version 0.11 Public API snapshot: generated list of public symbols and signatures, diffed in CI CI, docs/api.txt none An accidental API break fails the build 0.12 Schema registry (C1): every FSMDefinition field records the schema version that introduced it. synthesize is registered as 4.2 and the default version becomes "4.2". A definition that declares an older version but uses a newer field loads with a warning naming the field; fsm-llm-validate --upgrade rewrites the version core/definitions/schema.py C1 A test fails on any field missing from the registry 0.13 Reason codes (C8): core/codes.py holds statuses and reasons as str, Enum per the repo naming rules, with values equal to the existing synthesis wire strings; AgentResult.stop_reason, approval outcomes and completion results map into it core/codes.py C8 Every result type references the vocabulary; a test refuses unknown codes 0.14 State-kind registry (C2): the engine dispatches each state to the executor of its kind; State.kind is derived from the config the state carries, so the JSON shape does not change. conversation and completion are the first registered kinds; each kind supplies its verifier hooks engine/kinds/, core/verify/ C2, C6 The turn pipeline has no kind-specific branch outside executors; G3, G4 and G6a read kind hooks

docs.title: Phase 1: Durable, async runtime
docs.text:
Goal: every turn is an append-only sequence of events; sessions, monitor, metrics, usage, traces and evals are projections of it (C4).

Example event:

{"v": 1, "seq": 57, "ts": "2026-11-11T10:42:03.112Z", "conversation_id": "c_8f2", "frame": 1,
 "type": "llm/request", "pass": 1, "state": "collect_email", "model": "provider/model",
 "layout": {"prefix": "sha256:...", "history": "sha256:...", "suffix": "sha256:..."},
 "prompt_ref": "blob:sha256:..."}
# Change Where Builds on Done when 1.1 Append-only event log. Types: turn/start, llm/request, llm/response, provider/error, extraction, extraction/miss, intent/out_of_scope, transition, decision, handler, tool/call, tool/result, approval/request, approval/outcome, executor/start, executor/result, stack/push, stack/pop, context/record, compaction/epoch, turn/end. Large payloads are content-addressed blobs that also back value references (2.2). Single and batch append. A read-only history query API for handlers and agents runtime/events.py; engine/ emits C4 Any past prompt is rebuilt byte-identical from the log 1.2 Session persistence as projections: JSONL (optional zstd) and SQLite; versioned format with adjacent migrations; a reader for old FileSessionStore snapshots; completion transcripts included runtime/stores/ 1.1 A v1 to v2 migration test passes; old snapshots load; a completion state restored mid tool exchange continues 1.3 Checkpoint policy: durable write before every LLM call and every side-effecting tool call; a tool in flight during a crash recovers as unknown and is never retried automatically runtime/checkpoint.py 1.1 kill -9 mid-turn, restart, the conversation resumes with consistent history 1.4 API.fork(conversation_id, at_turn) and API.resume(conversation_id); fork and resume added to the verb list in the AGENTS.md naming conventions; time-travel view in the monitor engine/api, monitor/ 1.1, 1.2 A fork reproduces history up to the chosen turn 1.5 Async-first core. Async mirrors keep the sync names: LLMInterface.acomplete and the other interface methods, API.aconverse, API.aadvance, API.aconverse_stream, API.aadvance_stream, API.arun_until_terminal, API.arun_until_terminal_stream, Agent.arun, FSMSynthesizer.aobtain. Sync methods become wrappers. Per-turn cancellation token. A per-conversation lock replaces the documented "one thread per conversation" caller duty llm/, engine/api, agents/, synthesis/ C5 FastAPI serving without thread pools; concurrent calls on one conversation serialize; cancellation leaves a consistent log 1.6 Retry policy per provider, each attempt logged before backoff; admission control with shared pacing and overload cooldown across coroutines and processes runtime/retry.py, runtime/admission.py C5 Retries and throttling visible in the log; a load test against a rate-limited mock stays within limits 1.7 Core turn budgets: max_steps and max_seconds per conversation and per stack frame, enforced by the engine and reported as budget_spent (C8). The synthesis runner's own child-step counter is deleted engine/ C8, C9 A pushed frame over budget aborts through one path for any FSM, generated or not 1.8 Persist workflow instances on the log; a declarative step subset with a JSON loader for steps that hold no Python function workflows/ 1.1 A restarted process resumes a waiting workflow 1.9 Record and replay: fixtures keyed by a canonical request hash over the prompt layout segments (timestamps and ids excluded); replay fails on any unmatched request. Valid for refactors with unchanged definitions; definition changes need the simulator (6.6) testing/replay.py 1.1, 2.3 The replay suite runs keyless in default CI 1.10 OpenTelemetry spans generated from events, using the GenAI conventions pinned to a commit of semantic-conventions-genai; W3C trace context propagated into MCP _meta and A2A calls; the monitor reads the log instead of its own collector runtime/exporters/otel.py, monitor/ 1.1 One trace per turn with LLM spans and token counts; a call into an MCP server joins the trace 1.11 Log privacy levels: shape (default for shared stores: names, types, codes, counts) and values (opt-in); secret filters at write time; user-defined redaction; retention settings runtime/events.py, security.py C4 Secret-looking values never reach disk; a shape log holds no user text or reply (test) 1.12 ATIF v1.8 trajectory export generated from events runtime/exporters/atif.py 1.1 Exports validate with Harbor's trajectory validator on a Python 3.12+ CI leg 1.13 Usage as a projection: tokens, calls, cost and errors derive from llm/response and provider/error events; usage() reads the projection and reset_usage() moves a marker without dropping events runtime/usage.py, llm/ C4, C5 An outage during a synthesis run is reported as provider_error, even after reset_usage() or on an interface without its own meter

Exit criteria: crash-safe resume, fork, keyless replay in CI, usage and outages from events.

docs.title: Phase 2: Context engineering
docs.text:
Goal: the library knows what fills the context window, keeps large values out of it, and keeps prompts cache-valid so compaction is rare. Prevention (2.2 to 2.4) comes before cure (2.5).

# Change Where Builds on Done when 2.1 Token meter computed from events: pressure per layout segment and section; model catalog with context window, output limit, pricing (including cached input), reasoning-effort support llm/token_meter.py, llm/catalog.py C4 api.measure(conversation_id) returns a deterministic breakdown 2.2 Value references replace the fixed 2,000-character cap: any value over a size threshold (tool output, document, passage, large context value) is a blob held in context as a typed reference. Prompts render a bounded preview (type, size, head and tail, item count, depth); a read_ref tool pages through it; handlers, extraction and codeact receive the full value context/refs.py C4 The 50 KB skill is readable in 5 calls or fewer (now 37); a 1 MB tool result never enters a prompt in full 2.3 Prompt layout registry implementing Section 5.4: ordered sections inside prefix, history and suffix; scoped overrides; variables, where an unresolved variable fails the call; tool schemas in deterministic order. Trust rule: user, tool and retrieved text never enter the instruction sections context/layout/ (from prompts.py) C1, C2 Prompt diffs reviewable per section; injection test passes; Pass 1 and Pass 2 requests share a byte-identical prefix 2.4 Cache-valid transcripts: history is append-only; transitions, stack push and pop, and compaction epochs are appended as runtime-context records (harness pattern); the sliding max_history_size window is replaced by epochs; provider cache hints where supported context/layout/, llm/providers/* 2.3 The prefix hash is constant across a 20-turn conversation with transitions and a push and pop; cached-token share is reported per turn and gated against its first baseline 2.5 Compaction as a fallback and a cache epoch: triggered only when the token meter still shows pressure after 2.2 to 2.4; summarizes the oldest turns into a compaction/epoch record; overflow-recovery retry; ContextCompactor keeps key-level pruning context/compaction.py 2.1, 2.4 A long-conversation test survives at 90% of the window; at most one epoch per threshold crossing, each logged 2.6 Advisory repeat-tool-call reminder at 3, 5 and 8 identical consecutive calls, before the existing stalled stop agents/handlers.py none A loop test escapes without a forced stop 2.7 Opt-in AGENTS.md instruction handler with a byte budget and the untrusted label used for OKF context/instructions.py 2.3 Budget and labelling tested

Exit criteria: no silent truncation; no value above the reference threshold enters a prompt in full; the prefix is stable within an epoch.

docs.title: Phase 3: Knowledge and retrieval
docs.text:
Goal: conversations ground replies and routing in evidence, and routing reads evidence only as handler-only facts.

# Change Where Builds on Done when 3.1 fsm_llm[txtai] extra on the latest txtai release (9.14 today), with a canary job against txtai master: TxtaiMemoryBackend, create_txtai_tools(embeddings) retrieval/txtai.py 3.2 Agents search a txtai index with no glue code 3.2 VectorStore protocol with declared capabilities (upsert, delete, hybrid, calibrated_scores, metadata_filters); port SemanticMemoryStore; keep a dependency-free default. Recall scored by similarity, recency and importance, with consolidation that merges duplicates and prunes decayed entries retrieval/store.py, retrieval/memory.py C10 100k-entry search benchmarked and gated; a write the backend cannot perform is refused before any change; memory stays bounded in a long-run test 3.3 Hybrid (BM25 plus dense) search and metadata filters for OKF bundles okf/ 3.2 okf_search returns hybrid ranks 3.4 Retrieval as a state attribute of conversation states: before Pass 2 the retrieval executor writes the handler-only retrieval_result (status, top_score, coverage, calibrated, passages_ref); capped, labelled passages enter the suffix core/definitions, retrieval/executor.py C1, C2, C3 An example FSM answers from a bundle with citations 3.5 Evidence-aware routing on calibrated scores only, for example {">=": [{"var": "retrieval_result.top_score"}, 0.7]}. The verifier refuses a numeric threshold on top_score when the store does not declare calibrated_scores core/verify, retrieval/ 3.2, 3.4, C6 Routing tests without an LLM; the uncalibrated-threshold refusal is tested 3.6 fsm-llm-okf ingest <files> using txtai Textractor and Segmentation okf/ingest.py 3.1 PDFs and HTML become valid OKF bundles 3.7 Optional reranker step; a retrieval eval (recall@k, MRR) per bundle retrieval/rerank.py, eval/ 3.1 Measured lift reported 3.8 Retrieval hygiene: provenance and optional TTL on memory entries; retrieved text always carries the untrusted label retrieval/, security.py 2.3 Injection test: retrieved instructions are not followed 3.9 Decisions with confidence: tie-breaks and classifications write the handler-only decision_result (status decided or abstained, choice, confidence). A state may declare on_low_confidence (a state id) and a threshold, mirroring synthesize.on_failure; G4 checks that the abstain edge exists engine/transitions, classification.py, core/verify C1, C3, C6 A low-confidence tie-break routes to clarification in tests; calibration reported by 6.7

Exit criteria: a grounded FSM example with evidence- and confidence-gated routing passes offline tests and a live eval.

docs.title: Workstream O: FSMs as Python objects
docs.text:
Starts after Phase 0; O4 and O5 need Phase 1.

Goal: developers write FSMs the way NOOA writes agents (typed fields, docstrings, ... bodies) and get the same JSON definition, so the verifier, visualizer, monitor and synthesis keep working unchanged.

The rule that separates this from NOOA: routing compiles to JsonLogic. A guard outside the translatable subset is a compile error, never a runtime fallback.

from typing import Literal
from fsm_llm import API
from fsm_llm.oo import ConversationFSM, state, transition

class VisaIntake(ConversationFSM):
    """You are a concise visa intake assistant."""                  # persona

    passport_no: str | None = None                                  # context_schema (O1)
    purpose: Literal["tourism", "business", "study"] | None = None

    @state(initial=True, extracts=["passport_no"])
    def ask_passport(self) -> None:
        """Ask for the passport number and nothing else."""          # response_instructions
        ...                                                          # conversation kind: the LLM replies

    @transition(source="ask_passport", target="ask_purpose")
    def passport_given(self) -> bool:
        return self.passport_no is not None                          # {"!==": [{"var": "passport_no"}, null]}

    @state(extracts=["purpose"])
    def ask_purpose(self) -> None:
        """Ask the purpose of the trip."""
        ...

    @transition(source="ask_purpose", target="done")
    def purpose_given(self) -> bool:
        return self.purpose is not None

    @state(terminal=True)
    def done(self) -> str:
        return f"Recorded your {self.purpose} trip."                 # reply kind: template, no LLM call

definition = VisaIntake.compile()           # FSMDefinition JSON; the verifier (C6) runs here
api = API(definition, model="<small-model>")
conversation = await VisaIntake.start(api)  # O4: the conversation as a typed object
await conversation.converse("My passport number is X1234567")
conversation.passport_no                    # typed read of extracted context
Python construct Compiles to Class docstring persona Typed field (Optional[str], Literal[...], enum, Pydantic model, Field constraints) An entry in context_schema (JSON Schema) and an extraction target @state method with a ... body A conversation state; the docstring becomes response_instructions @state method whose body returns a string literal or an f-string over fields A reply state with a template; no LLM call @state(extracts=[...]) required_context_keys and field extractions for Pass 1 @transition(source, target, priority=...) guard A transition with JsonLogic logic; every key the guard reads is added to requires_context_keys @state(terminal=True) A terminal state @handler("name") or @tool("name") on a method with a real body A handler or tool registered by name (C10); the definition references the name

Translatable guard subset: reads of self.<field>; literals; comparisons (==, !=, <, <=, >, >=); is None and is not None (strict === and !==); and, or, not, bool(); in against literal collections or list fields; arithmetic; min, max; len(self.<field>) (mapped to context_length); and the helpers self.has(key), self.missing(*keys), self.missing_some(n, *keys) (mapped to has_context, missing, missing_some). Calls, loops, assignments and attribute access beyond fields fail to compile with the offending line named.

# Change Where Builds on Done when O1 Typed context schema: a context_schema field (JSON Schema) registered in the schema registry. Extraction is validated against it with bounded retry; the existing field_type values map onto it; types feed G3 core/definitions, engine/turn/pass1 0.12, C1 An invalid extraction is retried, then logged as extraction/miss; old definitions load unchanged O2 fsm_llm.oo compiler implementing the mapping and guard subset. Annotations are read with annotationlib (deferred evaluation, PEP 649 and 749) on 3.14 and later and typing.get_type_hints on 3.11 to 3.13. The reply state kind is registered with its verifier hooks oo/, engine/kinds/reply.py O1, 0.14, C10 Ten representative examples rewritten as classes compile to definitions equal to their JSON O3 Round trip: fsm_llm.oo.render(definition) and fsm-llm-meta --emit python produce a reviewable class from any definition, including synthesis library entries. Every JsonLogic operator the loader accepts has a Python rendering; an operator without one renders as a verbatim jsonlogic({...}) guard, which O2 accepts unchanged oo/render.py O2 Property test: JSON to class to JSON is identical for every example definition and every stored definition in the synthesis test corpus O4 Conversation as an object: start, resume, converse, advance, typed attribute reads, all backed by the event log oo/conversation.py O2, Phase 1 Kill the process, VisaIntake.resume(api, conversation_id), typed state intact O5 Optional fsm_llm[nooa] extra: NOOA agent methods callable from handlers and tools; an fsm_llm conversation exposed as an object a NOOA CodeAct method can drive. Environment markers restrict it to the Python versions and platforms NOOA supports (3.12 to 3.13, POSIX) agents/integrations/nooa.py O4 The interop example passes on a Linux CI leg; importing core never pulls in NOOA

docs.title: Phase 4: Agent harness capabilities
docs.text:
Goal: agents and executors that touch the outside world do so under one explicit, audited policy (C9).

# Change Where Builds on Done when 4.1 Policy and approval: modes ask (human or machine answerers), never (reject, for CI and unattended runs) and auto (a machine answerer such as an LLM reviewer; this roadmap's proposal). Permission presets; coded outcomes (C8); every request and outcome an event. Real HITL for REWOO, PlanExecute, ParallelReact and native_fc. synthesis.reviewer_from_hitl becomes a policy approver policy/, agents/ C8, C9, 1.1 Every gated call has an audited request and a coded outcome; a missing answerer fails closed 4.2 Sandbox seam with subprocess and container backends and an optional NVIDIA OpenShell backend; session-scoped writable directories; profiles referenced by the policy; PythonToolLoader runs tool files out of process policy/sandbox/ C9 Tool files run outside the host process; escape tests pass 4.3 Opt-in workspace toolset (read, write, edit, glob, grep, bash); read-only tools annotated concurrency-safe so executors may run them in parallel; writes gated by 4.1; paths confined by security.resolve_within tools/workspace.py 4.1 Path-escape, policy and parallel-read tests pass 4.4 Code as action on one sandboxed runtime with two program formats, mirroring harness protocol 3: program (one-shot; SDK generated from ToolRegistry, per-run call allowance, parallel-safe subcalls) and scoped-repl (persistent bindings; arguments by reference with previews; typed return_result validated against the declared output). Exposed as the codeact state kind writing codeact_result and as a codeact agent pattern. Environment initializers run before any model code. AST checks are defense in depth, never the boundary policy/sandbox/, agents/patterns/codeact.py, engine/kinds/codeact.py 2.2, 4.2, C2, C3 On a multi-tool suite codeact beats react and native_fc on success, or on tokens at equal success; a failing initializer prevents every program effect 4.5 Subagent tree: identity, depth limit, cancellation propagation, delivery to caller or parent; AgentGraph failure routing; the Orchestrator counts dropped subtasks agents/graph.py, agents/orchestrator.py 1.5, C8 A fallback branch can be built; cancel reaches all children; dropped subtasks lower success 4.6 Durable goal (one objective, round cap, compare-and-set updates), todo tool, plan mode as an FSM state with a human review gate agents/goal.py 1.1, 4.1 A goal survives restart 4.7 Layered skill registry: several providers with precedence; read-only, untrusted model kept skills/ C10 Duplicate skill names resolve predictably

Exit criteria: no agent or executor performs a side effect without a logged policy decision.

docs.title: Phase 5: Interop and serving
docs.text:
Goal: an FSM or agent is one config file away from a service any current client can call.

# Change Where Builds on Done when 5.1 Declarative app.yml (llm, fsms, agents, tools, memory, policy, api), Pydantic-validated; fsm-llm serve app.yml serve/app.py C9, C10 One file boots a full service 5.2 HTTP surfaces. Primary: an Open Responses-compatible POST /v1/responses, stateful through previous_response_id, with model naming an FSM or agent. Compatibility: /v1/chat/completions with a stated contract: the conversation id travels in metadata, only the final user message is consumed, and a request whose earlier messages disagree with the log is refused with a code. Streaming on both serve/responses.py, serve/chat.py 1.1, 1.5, C8 The Open Responses compliance suite passes for the supported subset; an OpenAI client drives an FSM through both routes 5.3 MCP 2026-07-28. Server: FSMs, agents and workflows as tools; a conversation tool returns conversation_id as an explicit handle; when a required key is missing, the call returns input_required carrying the state's question, and the host's retry with inputResponses becomes the next user turn (stateless slot filling); workflows and synthesis compiles run as Tasks; tool lists in deterministic order with cache hints. Client: streamable HTTP, legacy SSE removed before its deprecation window closes, mcp SDK 2.x serve/mcp.py, tools/mcp.py 1.10, 2.3, C3 A 2026-07-28 host fills a multi-slot FSM through MRTR with no session; any server instance behind a round-robin balancer can answer 5.4 Native providers: an Open Responses client (OpenAI, Ollama, vLLM, OpenRouter, LM Studio, Hugging Face) and an Anthropic Messages client; litellm becomes an extra, and tenacity leaves core with it llm/providers/ C5 Core installs and runs without litellm; provider conformance tests pass on recorded fixtures 5.5 Entry-point plugins (C10): fsm_llm.providers, fsm_llm.stores, fsm_llm.state_kinds, fsm_llm.tools, fsm_llm.handlers core/plugins.py, engine/ C10 A third-party package adds a provider and a state kind with no core edits 5.6 A2A v1.0.1 on a2a-sdk: parts without kind, agent card with supportedInterfaces, version header, trace context; ACP adapter later agents/a2a/ 1.10 Interop test against the A2A compatibility kit or reference implementation 5.7 Cron schedules for persisted workflows workflows/schedule.py 1.8 A scheduled workflow survives restart 5.8 AG-UI 1.0 event stream projected from the event log serve/agui.py 1.1 A reference UI renders a live FSM turn

Exit criteria: fsm-llm serve app.yml exposes one FSM over Open Responses, Chat Completions and MCP, all writing one event log.

docs.title: Phase 6: Evaluation as the headline
docs.text:
Goal: every quality claim is backed by a pre-registered, reproducible run on more than one model.

# Change Where Builds on Done when 6.1 Nightly live matrix: a hosted frontier model, a hosted mid-tier model and a small local model; budget cap; small subset nightly, full matrix weekly CI, eval/ 5.4 Results published per run 6.2 Verify end state, not text: final state, extracted context, transition path, <kind>_result codes, side effects; retire the 0 to 4 regex scorer eval/ C8, 1.1 Scores agree with manual review on a sampled set 6.3 Public FSM-conformance benchmark: scripted conversations, expected state paths, pass@k and pass^k with Wilson intervals via run_cases; hidden test split; per-model leaderboard eval/benchmark/ 6.2 Dataset and table published 6.4 Trace-to-eval: any values-level logged session becomes a regression case (deterministic parts replayed, user turns simulated) eval/, testing/ 1.11, 6.6 One CLI command 6.5 CI budgets on replay fixtures: LLM calls per turn, tokens per turn, cached-token share, framework overhead per turn (provider time excluded) CI 1.9, 2.4 A regression fails the build 6.6 One simulator (C7): promote synthesis.Simulator to simulation/; personas; goals seeded from logged sessions; paired, repeated comparisons; a judge model distinct from the executor and the compiler. G6b, repair admission and trace-to-eval use it simulation/ C7, 0.4 Simulated runs reproduce logged outcome rates within interval 6.7 Per-model capability tests: typed extraction per field type, tie-break choice and calibration, Pass 2 instruction following, typed return_result, synthesis compile success eval/capabilities/ 6.1 Capability table published per model 6.8 Benchmark discipline: the repo's pre-registration with sha256 source pins is required for every published number; each claim names the block that supports it; held-out tasks are never used to fix defects scripts/bench_data/, EVALUATE.md existing practice README quality claims cite a registered block run on at least three models

Exit criteria: README quality claims cite registered blocks on at least three models.

docs.title: 7. Phase 7: Runtime FSM synthesis, status and remaining work
docs.text: Subsections are numbered S1 to S10; remaining work items are P7.1 to P7.9.

docs.title: S1 Concept
docs.text: An agent acts as a compiler and the FSM is a verified program. When a conversation needs a structured sub-flow that no existing FSM covers, a strong model writes one, gates check it, and the host's model runs it as a pushed child. Successful FSMs go into a library and are reused, so the expensive step is paid once per kind of task. A declarative FSM can be checked before it runs, drawn for approval, versioned, cached by content hash and replayed on logged extractions, none of which a model-written script allows.

docs.title: S2 What shipped in v0.12.0
docs.text:
fsm_llm.synthesis: 5,881 lines in 16 modules, 2,037 tests, documented in src/synthesis/README.md and docs/synthesis.md.

v2.1 step Status Where M1 Synthesizer Shipped. FSMSynthesizer.compile and obtain (sync); one request per round; gate failures returned to the model as text for up to max_repair_rounds (3); a reply cut at max_tokens is a failed round; outages raise SynthesisError without retry synthesizer.py, prompts.py M2 Data flow and liveness Shipped in core, so every FSM can use them: G3 data flow; G4 traps, loops without a firing exit, edges hidden behind lower-priority unconditional edges, permanent ties, paths longer than max_turns src/flow_analysis.py M3 Policy and abort Shipped. G5 is an allow-list (unknown fields refused); injected abort terminal with a priority 0 edge from every non-terminal state, gated on the handler-only key procedure_abort policy.py M4 Library Shipped. Content-addressed by the sha256 of the canonical definition; lifecycle draft, verified, trusted, deprecated; signature filter, then exact goal match (no embedder) or cosine at or above reuse_min_score 0.8 (embedder); a hit is re-verified before it runs; atomic writes; symlinks refused library.py M5 Runtime integration Shipped. synthesize state field in the core schema; ProcedureRunner pushes the child with only the declared inputs, pops it, merges only the return keys and only on success; agent tools obtain_procedure and run_procedure runner.py, tools.py, definitions.py M6 Simulation gate Shipped as two gates: G6a (dead edges, dry run through the real evaluator, no model call) and G6b (scripted happy path plus model-written scenarios of four kinds) dryrun.py, simulation.py M7 Repair Shipped differently. Value-free run traces; nine diagnosis rules; RFC 6902 subset (add, remove, replace, test) scoped to diagnosed states; admission re-runs G1 to G6b and replays the parent's stored failing scenarios on parent and child; propose-only by default; a repaired child is never trusted traces.py, diagnose.py, patch.py, repair.py M8 Experiment Run: blocks s0, s1, s2, pre-registered and pinned to source hashes; all INCONCLUSIVE scripts/synthesis_bench.py, scripts/bench_data/synthesis/

docs.title: S3 Results to date
docs.text:
Model ollama_chat/bonsai-2:27b for every role and arm; 16 judge-free tasks in four families (collect, route, branch, retry); 3 trials each; primary unit is the first trial. S = synthesized FSM, H = hand-written FSM, R = ReAct.

Block S first trial (Wilson 95%) H first trial R first trial pass^3 S / H / R S tokens (prompt + completion) R tokens Verdict s0 6 of 16 (0.18 to 0.61) 8 of 16 14 of 16 6 / 8 / 12 826,182 + 186,111 536,759 + 92,680 INCONCLUSIVE (H below 10 of 16) s1 15 of 16 (0.72 to 0.99) 15 of 16 16 of 16 14 / 15 / 14 616,130 + 133,987 536,759 + 93,411 INCONCLUSIVE (ceiling) s2 15 of 16 (0.72 to 0.99) 16 of 16 16 of 16 15 / 15 / 15 613,642 + 130,506 536,759 + 92,601 INCONCLUSIVE (ceiling)

What this does and does not show:

  • No block shows a synthesized FSM beating ReAct. In s1 and s2 the arms are within one task on a saturated set.
  • With one model there is no strong and cheap split, so no cost saving could appear; S was the most expensive arm (compile plus more than 1,000 simulation calls per block). Reuse worked: 31 of 48 S rows in s1 and s2 made no compile call.
  • s1 and s2 ran on the same tasks after fixes made from earlier failures, so the gain from 6 to 15 of 16 is in-sample.
  • Two later fixes (D-108, D-109) have no registered block behind them.

docs.title: S4 Gates as shipped
docs.text: Gate Check Notes G1 Loads The JSON loads as FSMDefinition, exactly as API loads it Typed output (context_schema) added by P7.7 G2 Structure FSMValidator reports no error; warnings never fail Never stricter than the loader G3 Data flow Every key an edge reads is extracted earlier on every path or is a declared input; every return key is guaranteed at the end In core; documented blind spot for bulk-pass extraction G4 Liveness No trap, no loop without a firing exit, no hidden edge, no permanent tie, no path over max_turns In core G5 Policy Limits (12 states, 6 transitions per state, 10 fields per state, 600 characters per text); reserved names; no persona; no secret-looking or internal keys; no model settings; no regex; completion tools only from the allowlist; no nested synthesize at depth 1 Allow-list G6a Dead edges A small pool of values per key through the real evaluator; an edge no assignment can fire is reported Coarse by design; never rejects what it cannot read G6b Simulation Happy path and overall pass rate both at or above min_pass_rate (0.5), and the happy path moves past the first state Optional unless require_simulation; weak when the simulator shares the compiler's model G7 Approval Required by policy or when a completion state lists tools; the reviewer must return exactly True; fails closed Approval records provenance; trusted needs a separate library.approve

docs.title: S5 Interfaces as shipped, and the v3.0 target
docs.text:
As shipped:

from fsm_llm import API
from fsm_llm.synthesis import FSMLibrary, FSMSynthesizer, ProcedureRunner, SynthesisPolicy

synth = FSMSynthesizer(
    model="<strong-model>",
    library=FSMLibrary("~/.fsm_llm/library"),
    policy=SynthesisPolicy(require_approval=True),
    reviewer=reviewer,                          # callable(ProcedureApprovalRequest) -> bool
)
api = API.from_file("concierge.json", model="<small-model>")
runner = ProcedureRunner(api, host_definition, synth)
conversation_id, _ = api.start_conversation({"venue": "Luna"})
runner.converse(conversation_id, "four people, Friday")
runner.end_conversation(conversation_id)        # not API.end_conversation

"gather": {
  "id": "gather", "description": "run the procedure", "purpose": "collect", "response_instructions": "",
  "synthesize": {"goal": "Book a table: ask the party size and the date.",
                 "inputs": ["venue"], "return_keys": ["party_size", "visit_date"],
                 "on_failure": "sorry", "min_lifecycle": "verified"},
  "transitions": [
    {"target_state": "done", "description": "ok", "priority": 1,
     "conditions": [{"description": "ok", "requires_context_keys": ["synthesis_result"],
       "logic": {"==": [{"var": "synthesis_result.status"}, "ok"]}}]},
    {"target_state": "sorry", "description": "failed", "priority": 2,
     "conditions": [{"description": "failed", "requires_context_keys": ["synthesis_result"],
       "logic": {"in": [{"var": "synthesis_result.status"}, ["failed", "aborted"]]}}]}
  ]
}

Target after P7.1 (one driver, one API):

from fsm_llm.synthesis import SynthesizeExecutor

api = API.from_file("concierge.json", model="<small-model>", executors=[SynthesizeExecutor(synth)])
conversation_id, _ = api.start_conversation({"venue": "Luna"})
api.converse("four people, Friday", conversation_id)
api.end_conversation(conversation_id)

docs.title: S6 Divergences from the v2.1 design, resolved
docs.text: v2.1 design Shipped v3.0 decision Namespace fsm_llm.meta fsm_llm.synthesis Keep fsm_llm.synthesis; documented as experimental until S10 reports obtain(inputs=<data>) inputs are key names; values come from host context Keep names: the signature stays value-free and cacheable synthesize with goal_key, allowed_tools, library goal, inputs, return_keys, on_failure, result_key, min_lifecycle Keep shipped fields; tools stay in the policy, not the definition Async obtain Sync Add aobtain with 1.5 Counterfactual routing replay over logged extractions Impossible: traces hold no values by design Default stays scenario replay; counterfactual replay only on values-level logs (P7.8) G6 on the planned 6.6 user simulator Own Simulator in synthesis One simulator (C7, 6.6, P7.6) Synthesis runs inside the live conversation Separate ProcedureRunner driver; core leaves the state BLOCKED synthesize becomes a C2 executor (P7.1)

docs.title: S7 Remaining work
docs.text: # Change Where Builds on Done when P7.1 SynthesizeExecutor: ProcedureRunner becomes the executor of the synthesize kind in the engine registry; API.converse, advance and end_conversation drive it; without the executor registered, a definition with a synthesize state fails to load with a named error instead of blocking at run time synthesis/executor.py, engine/kinds/ 0.14, 1.7 The concierge example runs on bare API; the runner's own bookkeeping and end_conversation are removed P7.2 Library on the runtime store: records, run counters, traces, scenarios and patches become events and SQLite projections; counters update atomically across processes; a corrupt record is quarantined and reported instead of blocking retrieval for the whole library synthesis/library.py, runtime/stores/ 1.1, 1.2 Two processes on one library keep exact counters; a corrupted record leaves every other procedure retrievable P7.3 Signals from events: provider_error events replace the usage().errors heuristic; core emits extraction/miss and intent/out_of_scope; diagnosis gains rules for both synthesis/diagnose.py 1.1, 1.13 An outage is never diagnosed as a procedure fault; seeded out-of-scope and malformed-extraction defects are diagnosed P7.4 Lean imports: synthesis imports only L0 to L5 (tools, policy, simulation, engine); no import of agents, reasoning or eval synthesis/ 0.4, 6.6 The import-linter contract passes; import fsm_llm.synthesis loads no agent pattern P7.5 Tool-using procedures: completion states inside procedures run through the tool executor under the policy and sandbox; G5's allowlist and G7 stay mandatory synthesis/runner.py, engine/kinds/completion.py 4.1, 4.2 completion_unsupported is retired; a procedure that calls an allowlisted tool runs with an audited approval P7.6 Shared simulator and an independent judge: G6b and repair admission use simulation/ with a judge model different from the compiler synthesis/simulation.py → simulation/ 6.6 A gate report names the compiler, executor and judge models; same-model judging is refused unless explicitly allowed P7.7 Typed procedures: compile output carries context_schema; G3 checks types; approval requests show the definition rendered as a Python class synthesis/prompts.py, synthesis/synthesizer.py O1, O3 Compiled procedures validate extractions against their schema; the approval text includes the class rendering P7.8 Counterfactual routing replay, opt-in: on values-level logs, logged Pass 1 extractions are fed through the patched rules with no LLM call, exact up to the first divergence; the result is added to repair evidence synthesis/repair.py 1.11 A seeded routing defect is detected by replay before any simulation runs P7.9 Experiment v2 (S10) scripts/synthesis_bench.py P7.1 to P7.6, 6.1, 6.8 A registered block reports SUPPORTED or the falsifier fires

docs.title: S8 Trace-driven repair
docs.text:
Signal Likely defect Patch Dwell in one state for more than k turns Unsatisfiable or missing transition Add a transition or relax a condition High extraction/miss rate on one field Vague extraction instructions Rewrite instructions or split the field Frequent tie-breaks or low decision_result.confidence Ambiguous priorities Reorder priorities or add an abstain edge Abandonment concentrated in one state Poor step design Split the state or add a help path Frequent intent/out_of_scope Missing branch Add a state or route to a library FSM

Admission requires, in order: G1 to G6b on the patched child; replay of the parent's stored failing scenarios on parent and child (shipped); counterfactual routing replay when values logs exist (P7.8); a paired simulated comparison on the shared simulator (P7.6) in which the child must not lower the success rate and must improve the targeted failure. Whole-transcript replay is never used: once the bot's reply changes, recorded user turns no longer fit.

docs.title: S9 Security
docs.text:
As shipped, and kept:

  • The goal is untrusted caller text. It reaches the strong model only inside a fenced block, cut to 2,000 characters, control characters stripped, and [ ] < > replaced so it cannot spell a marker.
  • Model-written text never becomes a setting. G5 is an allow-list; persona, model, prompt settings and regular expressions are refused. Generated text shown to a model or a person carries a fixed untrusted label.
  • Return keys are the only way data leaves a child, and only on success. No goal, compile text, reply or provider text enters an exception, finding, result or trace.
  • The abort path hangs on a key no extraction can write.
  • Synthesis depth defaults to 1.
  • Repair needs positive evidence and a replay, and is propose-only by default.

Added in v3.0: every executed definition is recorded by hash in the event log (P7.2), so any conversation replays against the exact FSM it ran.

docs.title: S10 Experiment v2
docs.text: Item Design Hypothesis A small model running a frontier-compiled, verified FSM matches frontier ReAct on structured conversational tasks at a fraction of the cost Roles Compiler: hosted frontier model. Executor: small local model. Scenario writer and judge: a third model. Logged per row Tasks A fresh held-out set never used for fixes, in the four existing families plus harder ones: long slot sets, user corrections, multi-branch routing, tool use after P7.5; τ-bench-style domains with a user simulator and policy Arms Small ReAct; small model with the hand-written FSM; small model with an offline task-level FSM (MetaAgent-style); small model with a runtime-synthesized FSM; frontier ReAct Metrics pass^k, policy violations, stuck conversations, turns, total cost including compile cost amortized over library reuse, synthesis latency, library hit rate Ablations G3, G4, G6a, G6b on and off; library on and off; repair on and off Discipline Pre-registered with source pins (6.8); the verdict rule is fixed before the first row Falsifier If the runtime-synthesized arm does not beat the offline task-level arm on cost at equal success, the feature is scoped down to the verifier and library as developer tools

docs.title: 8. Novelty assessment
docs.text: Verdict: runtime FSM synthesis is not novel as a concept; every component has published prior art from 2024 to 2026. A narrow combination appears open. fsm_llm now has a working implementation of it, but its own benchmark has not separated it from ReAct, so it is a contribution only if experiment v2 (S10) supports it. As a library feature it is already distinctive: neither txtai, deepseek-harness nor NOOA offers it.

docs.title: 8.1 Prior art by component
docs.text:
Component Closest prior art Status LLM designs an FSM from a task description MetaAgent [1]: designs an FSM-based multi-agent system from a task description and lets the FSM control actions at deployment Done, per task FSM as the control structure for LLM task solving StateFlow [2]: higher success than ReAct at lower cost on InterCode SQL and ALFWorld; hand-designed machines Done, hand-designed One generated system per query at inference time FlowReasoner [3]: a reasoning meta-agent trained with execution feedback produces a system per query; code benchmarks Done, for code Static verification of a generated workflow before it runs Lean4Agent [4]: structural, semantic and trajectory verification in Lean4; Guardians [5]: plans with symbolic references verified against a security policy before any tool runs Done Plan library reused by a cheaper model Agentic Plan Caching [6]: plan templates extracted from past runs and adapted by a lightweight model Done Workflows induced from traces and composed Agent Workflow Memory [7]; WISE-Flow [8] for conversational service agents Done Gated self-repair with regression budget and lifecycle GRASP [9]; Self-Healing Harness [10] Done Executable dialogue logic from a flow description CoDial [11]: dialogue flow graph to Colang guardrail code Done, at design time Agent as a typed Python object whose ... methods an LLM completes NOOA [14] Prior art for Workstream O's authoring style, not for Phase 7 Replaying logged dialogues against a changed system Shown invalid for production dialogue agents [12] Constraint adopted in S8

Workstream O claims no novelty: class-based state machine declarations are common in Python FSM libraries, and the ... convention comes from NOOA. Its value is one canonical IR with two authoring surfaces. MCP slot filling through MRTR (5.3) is an application of the 2026-07-28 specification, not a research claim.

docs.title: 8.2 The open slice
docs.text:
No work found combines all four:

  1. Synthesis inside a live multi-turn conversation with a human, pushed onto a stack with a typed return contract, rather than per task or per code query.
  2. A rule-driven executor in which JsonLogic decides transitions and the LLM only extracts data and breaks ties.
  3. Slot-level static guarantees: data flow and liveness over extracted keys, including extraction failure.
  4. A frontier model compiles and a small model executes, measured on dialogue with a user simulator.

Items 1 to 3 are implemented. Item 4 has not been measured. Before any public claim, run a related-work pass over forward citations of [1], [4] and [6].

docs.title: 8.3 Claims
docs.text: Avoid Defensible only if S10 reports SUPPORTED "First agent that builds FSMs" "Runtime synthesis of verified dialogue state machines inside live conversations" "First verified workflow generation" "Slot-level liveness guarantees for LLM-driven dialogue FSMs" "First workflow caching" or "first self-improving workflows" "Frontier compiles, small model runs: X% of frontier success at Y% of cost on conversational tasks"
