docs.title: Architecture Deep Dive
docs.text:
Covers FSM-LLM v0.13.0

Technical overview of the FSM-LLM architecture and how components work together.

docs.title: System Overview
docs.text:
FSM-LLM uses a 2-pass architecture that separates data extraction, transition evaluation, and response generation:

  1. Pass 1 -- Analysis & Transition: Data extraction from user input, transition evaluation via JsonLogic rules (with LLM classification fallback for ambiguous cases), state transition.
  2. Pass 2 -- Response Generation: Response generated from the new state's context, ensuring the response always reflects the correct state.
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    User Application                   │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                     API Layer                         │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│   FSM Manager  │  Handler System  │  LLM Interface   │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│              MessagePipeline (2-pass)                 │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Prompt Builders  │  Context Manager  │  Evaluator   │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│   Storage: In-Memory Dicts (+ optional SessionStore)  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Conversation state lives in in-memory dicts by default. Attaching a SessionStore (e.g. FileSessionStore) adds durable, cross-restart persistence -- state is saved after each converse() and restored via restore_session().

docs.title: API (engine/api/)
docs.text: User-facing entry point. Manages FSM definition processing, component wiring, conversation lifecycle, and FSM stacking.

docs.title: FSMManager (engine/fsm/) + MessagePipeline (engine/turn/)
docs.text:
FSMManager handles FSM instance lifecycle with per-conversation thread locks and LRU FSM cache. MessagePipeline implements the 2-pass processing:

Pass 1: PRE_PROCESSING handlers → LLM extract data → CONTEXT_UPDATE handlers
      → Evaluate transitions → PRE_TRANSITION → State change → POST_TRANSITION

Pass 2: POST_PROCESSING handlers → LLM generate response → Return

docs.title: Prompt Builders (context/layout/)
docs.text:
Two builders produce structured XML-like prompts, plus the Pass-1 builder slot: - DataExtractionPromptBuilder -- the Pass-1 slot of FSMManager/MessagePipeline; the pipeline builds the bulk extraction prompt inline and uses this builder only for the shared sanitizer - ResponseGenerationPromptBuilder -- Pass 2: user-facing response generation - FieldExtractionPromptBuilder -- Targeted single-field extraction

Security: XML tag sanitization, CDATA wrapping for JSON, token budget management.

docs.title: Handler System (handlers/)
docs.text: Plugin architecture with 8 timing points. Handlers self-determine execution via state/context conditions, execute in priority order, with configurable error isolation ("continue" or "raise"). Critical handlers always raise on error.

docs.title: LLM Interface (llm/)
docs.text:
LLMInterface ABC with the methods: - generate_response(request) -- Generate user-facing response (Pass 2) - extract_field(request) -- Extract a targeted field from input (Pass 1) - generate_response_stream(request) -- Stream the Pass-2 response token-by-token - extract_bulk_data(request) -- Bulk extraction for states with extraction_instructions - complete(request: CompletionRequest) -> CompletionResponse -- The one primitive for tool calling, plain and structured completion (classifier, completion states, the agents' LLM judge). Not abstract: the base method raises NotImplementedError

LiteLLMInterface provides the built-in implementation supporting 100+ providers. It is the one place a provider request is built (_build_call_params) and sent (one send path that counts every call on the instance: usage()), for every call kind; LiteLLMEmbedder is the one embedding path. litellm is imported in exactly one module, llm/providers/litellm.py; nothing else in the package (agents, reasoning, meta-builder) calls a provider by itself. The classifier of a conversation sends its complete requests through the conversation's own llm_interface. Request models carry user_message: str | None; the request builder sends None (no user message) as the fixed NEUTRAL_USER_TURN and an empty or whitespace message as EMPTY_USER_MESSAGE_TURN, so the provider never sees an empty user turn and never reads an empty message as an instruction.

docs.title: TransitionEvaluator (core/transition_evaluator.py)
docs.text:
Three-outcome evaluation: - DETERMINISTIC -- One passing transition, or a unique lowest priority value among several passing ones, proceed automatically - AMBIGUOUS -- Two or more passing transitions tied at the lowest priority; only the tied group is delegated to LLM classification - BLOCKED -- No matches, stay in current state

Uses JsonLogic conditions (core/expressions/) and required context key checks.

docs.title: Message Processing
docs.text:
User Message → API.converse()
  → FSMManager.process_message() [acquires per-conversation lock]
    → MessagePipeline.process()
      → PRE_PROCESSING handlers
      → LLM: extract data from user input
      → Update context (merge extracted data)
      → CONTEXT_UPDATE handlers (if keys changed)
      → TransitionEvaluator: evaluate transitions
      → If transitioning: PRE_TRANSITION → state change → POST_TRANSITION
      → POST_PROCESSING handlers
      → LLM: generate response from NEW state
    → Return response

docs.title: Steps Without a User Message (API.advance, API.run_until_terminal)
docs.text:
API.advance(conversation_id)
  → FSMManager.advance() [same per-conversation lock and turn guard]
    → MessagePipeline.advance() → the same turn body as process(), user_message=None
      → no user exchange appended to history
      → Pass 1 prompts in their no-message wording (bulk prompt built from the
        scoped, security-filtered context; fills unset keys only)
      → transition evaluation and Pass 2 exactly as for a message
    → Return AdvanceResult(state_before, state_after, transition_outcome, response, ended)

API.run_until_terminal(conversation_id, *, max_steps, max_seconds=None, before_step=None,
                       seconds_exempt_states=())
  → per round: ended? → seconds budget → steps budget → before_step(n) → advance()
  → an ended PUSHED FSM on top: before_step(n) once (not a step) so the hook can pop it;
    the run then continues on the parent, or returns if nothing was popped
  → RunBudgetExceededError when a budget is spent; a conversation closed mid-run ends it normally

This is how the agents, the reasoning engine and any program that drives an FSM by itself run a conversation: no synthetic user message is ever sent. The reasoning engine runs one orchestrator run whose before_step hook pushes and pops the strategy FSMs. advance_stream and run_until_terminal_stream are the streaming forms (reply text only).

docs.title: Completion States (tool calling and structured output)
docs.text:
State with "completion": {tools | response_format_key, tool_choice, instructions,
                          messages_key, result_key}
  Pass 1 → one LLMInterface.complete() over [system(instructions)] + context[messages_key]
         → context[result_key] = {kind: calls | final | malformed, text, calls: [{id, name, arguments}]}
  transitions read <result_key>.kind; a handler runs the calls, appends
  tool_exchange(content, calls, results) to the transcript and clears result_key

The transcript is a context list the consumer owns (an internal key), never the conversation history. Core runs no tool, adds no prompt text and no history, and refuses an unpaired transcript with LLMResponseError before sending (the turn rolls back). NativeFunctionCallingReactAgent (tool loop, forced final tool, repair turn) and the meta-builder's build call are completion states.

docs.title: Synthesize States (procedures written on demand)
docs.text:
State with "synthesize": {goal, inputs, return_keys, on_failure, result_key, min_lifecycle}
  Pass 1 → no extraction; the pipeline makes result_key handler-only
  ProcedureRunner (before_step hook of run_until_terminal, or around converse):
    start   → write {status: running} → obtain(goal) → library hit, or compile + gates G1 to G7
            → push_fsm(child, inherit_context=False) with only the declared inputs
    tick    → a child over policy.max_turns steps gets procedure_abort set (priority 0 abort edge)
    finish  → pop_fsm(context_to_return=return_keys) only on success
            → context[result_key] = {status: ok | failed | aborted, procedure_id, version, reason}
  transitions read <result_key>.status

Core only loads the field and checks the host FSM with the real evaluator (every edge reads the result, none fires before the runner has written one, the failure edge passes for failed and aborted). The runner is a consumer of the public step driver, as the reasoning engine is: it adds no seam to core. A bare API.converse on a synthesize state stays in it. See synthesis.md.

docs.title: State Kinds and Executors
docs.text:
A state has exactly one kind, derived from the config it carries: conversation (the default: field, bulk and classification extraction, then a reply), completion (a completion config) or synthesize (a synthesize config). State.kind returns the name. It is a plain read-only property, not a field: it is absent from model_dump, model_fields and the JSON schema, so a definition cannot declare it and no fsm_id or library digest moves.

The extension point has two halves, and a new kind needs both:

  • Declaration (core). A frozen KindSpec in fsm_llm.core.state_kinds names the kind, the State field that carries its config (config_field) and the rules the rest of core reads: result_key, inherits_result_on_push, forbidden_declarations, check_state, check_definition and sample_results (the loader), dryrun_judged, mentioned_keys and typed_keys (gate G6a), minted_keys and produced_keys (the pipeline, G3 and G4), lint_raw and raw_result_key (the validator, which reads raw dicts), declared_tools, raw_declared_tools and supported_in_procedure (synthesis). The registry (KINDS, kind_of, get_kind) is static and process-wide; fsm_llm.core.state_kinds is a leaf that imports only the standard library.
  • Execution (engine). A StateExecutor in fsm_llm.engine.kinds says what the kind does in Pass 1: extract(...) produces the turn's extraction result, cleans_extracted says whether the data goes through clean_context_keys, and after_transition(...) runs when a transition lands in a state of the kind. The pipeline picks the executor with executor_for(state, executors) at the one Pass-1 seam that the sync and the stream path share. The executor table is per instance: API(..., executors={kind_name: executor}), passed down to FSMManager and MessagePipeline, is validated, copied read-only and visible to that API only. A kind with no executor (synthesize, which is passive, or a runtime kind nobody registered) runs as conversation, resolved through that API's own conversation entry first and the module's second, so an executors={"conversation": X} override covers it too (a bare converse on a synthesize state stays in it, as before).

What the engine guarantees to an executor: process() takes the one snapshot of the turn and restores it on a failure (see Turn atomicity in src/fsm_llm/AGENTS.md), so an executor takes none of its own; handler-only keys (a kind's result_key) are never minted as extraction targets; Pass 2 stays shared and kind-agnostic. What it does not: the conversation Pass-1 methods (_extract_after_transition, _execute_data_extraction and their field, bulk and classification helpers) still live on MessagePipeline and the conversation executor calls them; they move with the module layout split (roadmap 0.4), they were not deleted. A test-only kind registered at runtime runs a full conversation with no edit in core (tests/test_fsm_llm/test_executor_map.py).

Nothing here is public yet: fsm_llm/__init__.py exports neither module, executors= is not on the builders, and the entry-point group for third-party kinds arrives with the plugin work (roadmap C10, row 5.5). Until then both packages (core.state_kinds and engine.kinds) are internal. The executors keyword of API, FSMManager and MessagePipeline shows in the API snapshot fixture (tests/fixtures/api_snapshot.txt) as Mapping[str, StateExecutor] | None: StateExecutor is imported from fsm_llm.engine.kinds (not from fsm_llm) and is internal until the kind registry is exported, so the annotation names a class the package does not export, on purpose.

docs.title: Conversation Start
docs.text:
API.start_conversation(initial_context)
  → FSMManager: create FSM instance
  → START_CONVERSATION handlers
  → MessagePipeline: generate initial response from initial state
  → Return (conversation_id, response)

docs.title: Streaming (API.converse_stream)
docs.text:
API.converse_stream() → MessagePipeline.process_stream()
  → Pass 1 runs fully (extract → transition), identical to the synchronous path
  → Pass 2 streams the response token-by-token via LLMInterface.generate_response_stream()
  → yields str chunks to the caller

States with an empty response_instructions skip Pass 2 entirely: no LLM call, the empty reply ("" from start_conversation/converse, no chunk from a stream, response=None from advance) and nothing added to the history. This is the common shape for intermediate agent/tool-dispatch states.

docs.title: Context Handling
docs.text:
class FSMContext:
    data: dict           # User-defined context (extracted data, handler outputs)
    conversation: Conversation  # Message history with max_history_size
    metadata: dict       # System metadata
    working_memory: WorkingMemory  # Named buffers (core, scratch, environment, reasoning)

get_user_visible_data() (which merges the non-hidden buffers into data, minus internal keys and secret-looking entries; the one key policy lives in security/, so a key named exactly system is an ordinary visible key, unlike system_*) enters the Pass-1 per-field extraction prompt (_execute_field_extractions, when a field's context_keys is left at its default) and both classifier call sites. The three Pass-2 sites (_execute_response_generation_pass, _stream_response_generation_pass, and generate_initial_response when a greeting is generated) build the <current_context> block from get_merged_data(), scoped by read_keys; the prompt is the only context channel, since ResponseGenerationRequest carries no context field. update_context/handlers write data only; a value that must reach the shipped response prompt belongs in data. working_memory is also exclude=True, so FSMContext.model_dump() omits it (sessions persist it through WorkingMemory.to_dict()).

Special keys (prefixed with _): _conversation_id, _conversation_start, _fsm_id, _timestamp, and, once a transition has happened, _current_state, _previous_state, _transition_timestamp. ERROR handlers additionally see _error and _traceback. Formats: _conversation_start is naive local-time ISO text (datetime.now().isoformat()), _timestamp and _transition_timestamp are epoch seconds (floats), and none of the three is persisted by save_session (UTC-aware values are carried, not built). The raw user message is not in the context, so handlers see extracted keys only.

docs.title: Context in Stacked FSMs
docs.text: On push_fsm: parent context optionally inherited/passed to child. On pop_fsm: only what was declared is merged back into the parent, the child's other keys are dropped: the child's values for shared_context_keys, plus the return_context given to push_fsm and the context_to_return given to pop_fsm. The merge strategy only decides collisions on those keys: - UPDATE -- Returned value overwrites the parent's - PRESERVE -- Only keys the parent does not have yet are added

docs.title: Handler Execution Pipeline
docs.text:
START_CONVERSATION → [per message: PRE_PROCESSING → extract → CONTEXT_UPDATE
→ evaluate → PRE_TRANSITION → transition → POST_TRANSITION → POST_PROCESSING
→ generate response] → END_CONVERSATION. ERROR on an exception raised while processing a message (`converse` / `converse_stream`; not for a failure inside `start_conversation`).

Priority ordering (lower first). Error modes: "continue" (log + skip) or "raise" (propagate). Critical handlers always raise.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Prompt injection prevention: XML tag sanitization on all user input
  • Context isolation: Per-conversation isolated state, no cross-conversation access
  • Input validation: Length limits, sanitization
  • Forbidden patterns: Regex filtering for passwords, secrets, API keys, tokens
  • Internal key prefixes: _, system_, internal_, __ stripped from user-facing context

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
• Conversation history limits: max_history_size (default 5) is the number of exchanges stored per conversation and also the number of messages the extraction and response prompts show (the last N, passed unchanged to the default prompt builders, so the unit of the shown window is messages); the history token budget (default 3000) can cut the window below N, so at most N messages are shown. max_message_length (default 1000)
  • FSM definition caching: LRU cache (max 64) for loaded definitions
  • Handler pre-filtering: Only check handlers matching current timing
  • Thread safety: Per-conversation RLocks in FSMManager

docs.title: Package Layout
docs.text:
The library is one import package, fsm_llm, in src/fsm_llm/. Beneath the seven extension subpackages sit layer packages that ship with every install, and a layer imports only the layers below it. The rule is enforced by .importlinter (make lint-imports, and the test tests/test_fsm_llm_regression/test_import_contract.py), and no module is over 800 lines.

Layer (top to bottom) Packages What it holds Subpackages monitor, eval; agents, synthesis, workflows, reasoning; testing One extra each, imported by name, never by import fsm_llm engine fsm_llm.engine API (engine.api), FSMManager (engine.fsm), the 2-pass MessagePipeline (engine.turn), the state-kind executors (engine.kinds), Classifier, the builders, the session store, the plain-FSM OKF handler (engine.okf_bridge) handlers fsm_llm.handlers The handler system, HandlerBuilder, create_handler policy fsm_llm.policy Approval types and the human-in-the-loop manager; imports tools and none of context, okf, skills (the contract policy-imports-no-sibling-layer: the row sits above the siblings, so only the contract keeps it off them) Independent siblings context, okf, skills, tools Context compaction and prompt builders (context.layout); Open Knowledge Format; Agent Skills; the tool registry and tool models llm fsm_llm.llm LLMInterface, LiteLLMInterface (the one litellm import), the embedder, reply parsing core fsm_llm.core Pydantic FSM models (core.definitions), JsonLogic (core.expressions), core.transition_evaluator, core.state_kinds, core.verify (validator, data-flow and liveness analyses), core.visualize Kernel constants, logging, security, text, env, frontmatter, memory, cli_support Small modules any layer may import; they import no layer

import fsm_llm loads the core, engine, handlers, context, llm and security packages and a few kernel modules, and nothing else: no subpackage and none of okf, skills, tools or policy (pinned by tests/test_fsm_llm_regression/test_import_laziness.py). Three edges break the order on purpose and are named in .importlinter: agents imports reasoning (for ReasoningReactAgent), and synthesis imports agents.semantic_tools and eval (the simulator reuses the scripted-trial code).

docs.title: Extension Integration
docs.text:
fsm_llm (core, includes classification)
├── fsm_llm.reasoning  -- Uses API run_until_terminal; its before_step hook pushes/pops strategy FSMs
├── fsm_llm.workflows  -- Uses API (via ConversationStep); lifecycle hooks via add_hook
├── fsm_llm.agents     -- Uses API (auto-generates FSMs, drives them with run_until_terminal)
│                          + handlers for tool execution; native_fc and the meta-builder use completion states
├── fsm_llm.monitor    -- Uses API + handlers (observer callbacks at priority 9999)
├── fsm_llm.eval       -- Runs example scripts as subprocesses; drives scripted conversations
│                          through API (one instance per trial) and checks the outcome
├── fsm_llm.synthesis  -- Uses API (push_fsm/pop_fsm, run_until_terminal's before_step hook), agents
│                          (tools, human approval) and eval (scripted trials for simulation); core
│                          loads its `synthesize` state field and runs the data-flow and liveness
│                          analyses (`core/verify/flow.py`)
└── fsm_llm.testing    -- Public test doubles, scripted user and assertions; imports core only

The seven extensions are subpackages of fsm_llm. Core never imports them at package import time; each one imports core (from fsm_llm import API). Their place among the layers is in Package Layout above.

Package Integration Key Mechanism Classification Built into core Structured complete call through the conversation's llm_interface Reasoning One message-free run + FSM stacking run_until_terminal on the orchestrator; the before_step hook pushes a strategy FSM by type and pops it when it ends (or after 30 steps); a spent 170-step budget raises ReasoningExecutionError Workflows Async engine + ConversationStep ConversationStep creates API instance for FSM conversations Agents Auto-generated FSMs + handlers, driven by core run_until_terminal build_react_fsm() generates FSM; handlers execute tools on state entry; core owns the step and time budgets; no synthetic message is sent. native_fc runs on core completion states (native tool calls); the meta-builder is an FSM driven with converse/advance. Also covers multi-agent graph/swarm orchestration, MCP tools, A2A remote agents, and semantic tool retrieval Monitor Observer handlers + loguru sink + core graph data Registers observer handlers (priority 9999; not POST_TRANSITION), never modifies state; FSM graphs come from build_fsm_graph Eval Subprocesses + public API only fsm-llm-eval examples scores example output with a 0-4 heuristic; fsm-llm-eval run sends each case's turns through a fresh API, reads get_current_state/get_data/has_conversation_ended, and checks declared expectations over N trials. No handlers, no core changes Synthesis A silent synthesize state + a runner on the core step driver A model compiles a goal into an FSM, gates G1 to G7 judge it, a content-addressed library stores it, and ProcedureRunner pushes it as a child (no inherited context), runs it on the host model and merges back only the declared return keys. Core adds the synthesize state field, the loader checks of its edges and core/verify/flow.py; no handler and no second engine

docs.title: Custom LLM Interface
docs.text:
from fsm_llm.constants import NEUTRAL_USER_TURN

class CustomLLM(LLMInterface):
    def generate_response(self, request: ResponseGenerationRequest) -> ResponseGenerationResponse:
        # user_message is None when there is no user message (a message-free
        # step, a greeting); "" or any string is what the user sent. A silent
        # state (empty response_instructions) never reaches this method.
        user_turn = request.user_message if request.user_message is not None else NEUTRAL_USER_TURN
        response = your_api(request.system_prompt, user_turn)
        return ResponseGenerationResponse(message=response)

    def extract_field(self, request: FieldExtractionRequest) -> FieldExtractionResponse:
        ...

    def extract_bulk_data(self, request: BulkExtractionRequest) -> DataExtractionResponse:
        ...  # needed by states with extraction_instructions; the base class raises NotImplementedError

    def complete(self, request: CompletionRequest) -> CompletionResponse:
        ...  # needed by classification and completion states; API refuses a definition with
             # classification_extractions when this is not implemented

docs.title: Custom Handlers
docs.text:
class DatabaseHandler(BaseHandler):
    def should_execute(self, timing, current_state, target_state, context, updated_keys):
        return timing == HandlerTiming.POST_TRANSITION

    def execute(self, context):
        database.save(context["_conversation_id"], context)
        return {"saved_to_db": True}

docs.title: State Kinds (internal)
docs.text: A new state kind is a KindSpec in fsm_llm.core.state_kinds plus a StateExecutor supplied with executors={kind_name: executor} on API, FSMManager or MessagePipeline; see State Kinds and Executors above. It is not a public extension point yet: no export from fsm_llm, no builder setter, no entry-point group before roadmap row 5.5.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
Covers FSM-LLM v0.13.0

The distribution installs one console script per tool, all prefixed fsm-llm, and the reasoning engine has one more entry that is run as a module. Each section gives the entry point (the module:function of [project.scripts] in pyproject.toml), what it is for and its usage. --help on any of them prints every option.

docs.title: Common rules
docs.text:
Model. The model is never built in. The CLIs that call one (fsm-llm, fsm-llm-eval, fsm-llm-meta, python -m fsm_llm.reasoning) take --model (-m on fsm-llm and the reasoning CLI), then the process environment variable LLM_MODEL, then the file named by --env-file. With none of the three they exit 1 with one message on stderr (ModelNotConfiguredError). fsm-llm-monitor starts without a model: LLM_MODEL reaches its launch routes, which answer 400 when none is set.

--env-file PATH. Importing fsm_llm reads no .env file. The five model CLIs (fsm-llm, fsm-llm-eval, fsm-llm-meta, fsm-llm-monitor, python -m fsm_llm.reasoning) take one flag, --env-file PATH, that loads the file into the environment first. A variable the process already has wins; a blank one counts as unset; a missing file is one stderr line and exit 1. The CLIs that call no model (fsm-llm-validate, fsm-llm-visualize, fsm-llm-okf, fsm-llm-skills) do not take it.

Exit codes. 0 is success, 1 is a failure, 130 is Ctrl-C. A usage error exits 2 (argparse), except in fsm-llm-eval, which exits 1 for it. fsm-llm-eval exits 2 only when the score is below --fail-under PCT.

docs.title: fsm-llm
docs.text:
Entry point: fsm_llm.__main__:main_cli.

Runs an FSM definition as an interactive conversation, or validates or draws it with --mode validate and --mode visualize. Running needs a model.

fsm-llm --fsm <path.json> [--model M] [--env-file PATH]

Other options: --mode {run,validate,visualize}, --style {full,compact,minimal}, --history-size N (exchanges kept, default 5), --message-length N (default 1000) and --version.

docs.title: fsm-llm-validate
docs.text:
Entry point: fsm_llm.core.verify.cli:main_cli.

Validates an FSM definition file. --upgrade validates first and then rewrites a definition that declares version 4.0 up to below the current one to the current version; it exits 1 when the upgrade is refused or fails. Calls no model.

fsm-llm-validate --fsm <path.json> [--upgrade]

docs.title: fsm-llm-visualize
docs.text:
Entry point: fsm_llm.core.visualize.cli:main_cli.

Draws an FSM definition as an ASCII, Mermaid or DOT diagram. --style applies to ASCII only. Calls no model.

fsm-llm-visualize --fsm <path.json> [--format ascii|mermaid|dot] [--style full|compact|minimal]

docs.title: fsm-llm-monitor
docs.text:
Entry point: fsm_llm.monitor.__main__:main_cli.

Starts the web dashboard (REST, WebSocket and a single-page app) at http://127.0.0.1:8420. Needs the monitor extra. --api-key (or the FSM_LLM_MONITOR_API_KEY variable) guards the mutating and sensitive routes; --otel exports monitor events as OpenTelemetry spans.

fsm-llm-monitor [--host HOST] [--port PORT] [--no-browser] [--api-key KEY] [--otel] [--env-file PATH]

Also --info and --version, which print and exit.

docs.title: fsm-llm-meta
docs.text:
Entry point: fsm_llm.agents.meta_cli:main_cli.

An interactive builder: a conversation that produces an FSM, workflow or agent definition as a JSON artifact. Needs a model.

fsm-llm-meta [--model M] [--env-file PATH] [--output FILE] [--temperature T] [--max-turns N]

docs.title: fsm-llm-eval
docs.text:
Entry point: fsm_llm.eval.__main__:run.

Two commands. examples runs the repository examples and scores each 0 to 4; run plays scripted conversations against an FSM, N trials each, and reports pass rates with Wilson confidence intervals. Both need a model and write their results under evaluation/. Settings precedence is defaults, then the dataset config, then --config FILE, then flags. With one model server slot use --workers 1.

fsm-llm-eval examples [--category C] [--fail-under PCT] [--env-file PATH]
fsm-llm-eval run <dataset.json|.jsonl> [--trials N] [--env-file PATH]

Exit codes differ from the common rule: a usage error exits 1, and exit 2 means the score fell below --fail-under PCT.

docs.title: fsm-llm-okf
docs.text:
Entry point: fsm_llm.okf.cli:main_cli.

Works with Open Knowledge Format bundles. Calls no model.

fsm-llm-okf <validate|list|show|search|export> ...

validate checks a bundle (--strict), list lists its concepts, show prints one concept, search searches titles, tags and bodies, and export writes a semantic-memory JSON file as a bundle. Every command except export takes --max-seconds.

docs.title: fsm-llm-skills
docs.text:
Entry point: fsm_llm.skills.cli:main_cli.

Reads Agent Skills folders (SKILL.md). It is read-only and runs nothing from a skill. Calls no model.

fsm-llm-skills <validate|list|show> PATH...

validate --strict is the strict check; show NAME PATH... prints a skill body, or one bundled file with --file RELPATH.

docs.title: python -m fsm_llm.reasoning
docs.text:
Entry point: fsm_llm.reasoning.__main__ (run as a module: the reasoning CLI has no console script).

Solves a problem with one of the reasoning strategies and prints the answer with a trace. Needs a model.

python -m fsm_llm.reasoning "problem" [--type T] [--model M] [--env-file PATH]

Other options: --context JSON, --output text|json|detailed, --save FILE, --verbose, --quiet, --list-types and --version.
